Find the $y$-coordinate of the points on the curve $y={x}^{2}-4x$ that are closest to the point $(2,0).$
question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(2,0)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =(x-2)^{2}+{y}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-4x+4+{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y={x}^{2}-4x.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(y) & ={x}^{2}-4x+4+{y}^{2} \\  & =y+4+{y}^{2} \\  & ={y}^{2}+y+4.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(y)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(y)=2y+1 & =0 \\ 2y & =-1 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(y)=2>0.$ Therefore, $y=-\frac{1}{2}$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $y=-\frac{1}{2}.$
